name: StrucTab-Bench
description: Accurate table recognition requires complete recognition of cell content and logical structure, which provides a foundation for table understanding and reasoning. However, complex table recognition remains challenging: existing training datasets contain limited complex examples and insufficient diversity, while commonly used similarity metrics mainly measure local matching and do not directly indicate whether an entire table is functionally correct. In this work, functional correctness means that the evaluated table content, cell order, and logical topology exactly match the reference after canonicalization. To address these problems, we introduce StrucTab, a data resource comprising StrucTab-Train, with approximately 633K bilingual image–HTML pairs, and StrucTab-Bench, a benchmark of 425 real complex scientific tables. We also introduce Table-Level Correctness (TLC), which formalizes this functional-correctness criterion as a canonicalized whole-table exact-match measure. Experiments show that StrucTab-Train effectively improves complex scientific table recognition: after fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3.5-9B, TLC exceeds the best alternative training dataset by 5.65 percentage points for each backbone. Nevertheless, the highest TLC on StrucTab-Bench is only 24.94%, despite much higher similarity scores.
